segments.he: וְאִם נָפַל מֵרוּקָּהּ. דִּתְנַן: מַשְׁקֵה טְבוּל יוֹם מַשְׁקִין הַיּוֹצְאִין מִמֶּנּוּ (כְּמַשְׁקִין) [כְּמַשְׁקֶה] הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶם, וְאֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ אֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין, חוּץ מִמַּשְׁקֵה הַזָּב שֶׁהוּא אַב הַטּוּמְאָה.
segments.en: The mishna teaches: «And» Beit Shammai concede to Beit Hillel that «if» a drop «from her saliva» or from the blood of purity fell onto a loaf of teruma, that the loaf is ritually pure, as any liquid discharged from the body of one who immersed that day is ritually pure. The Gemara explains that the reason is «as we learned» in a mishna (Tevul Yom 2:1): The halakha with regard to «liquids» that emerge «from one who immersed himself that day» from his state of ritual impurity «is like» that of «liquids that he touches. And» both «these and those,» the liquids that emanated from him and the liquids that he touched, «do not transmit ritual impurity.» This is the halakha «except for liquids» that come «from a zav, who is a primary source of ritual impurity.»
